newsitem.title: GERMANY: OECD says may revise German 96 GDP forecast up.
newsitem.headline: OECD says may revise German 96 GDP forecast up.

text.p: The Organisation for Economic Cooperation and Development (OECD) said on Thursday it would probably revise up its forecast for German 1996 growth in the wake of strong first half figures.

"Our forecast is likely to go up to a rise of between 0.5 and what the Economics Minister has predicted," OECD representative in Germany Dieter Menke told reporters while presenting the organisation's annual report on Germany.
The report predicted a GDP rise of 0.5 percent for 1996. Economics Minister Guenter Rexrodt has forecast growth of 0.75 percent.

Earlier on Thursday official data showed GDP rose more strongly than expected in the second quarter and first half of the year. Rexrodt said the government might raise its forecast for the full year from its previous 0.75 percent projection.
Menke said the revision would probably be made in October.
German GDP grew 0.7 percent in the first half of 1996 from the same year earlier period. The OECD's report predicted a fall of 0.3 percent. -- Ashley Seager, Bonn newsroom, 49-228-2609750
